line.friends.gift.loved.1: Oh! How did you know I adore this? Thank you!
line.friends.gift.loved.2: {0}, you do spoil me! This is my very favourite.
line.friends.gift.loved.3: Now that's a present! Straight to the heart.
line.friends.gift.loved.4: {0}, thank you! Now the whole day's going to be good, no doubt about it.
line.friends.gift.loved.5: How did you guess? It's exactly what today was missing.
line.friends.gift.liked.2: {0}, you shouldn't have... But thank you, it'll come in handy.
line.friends.gift.liked.4: Oh, thank you, {0}! That's cheered me up already.
line.friends.gift.liked.5: A present? For me? Well, I never. Thank you.
line.friends.gift.plain.1: Thank you... It's not really my sort of thing, to be honest. But I'll pass it on to someone who'll be glad of it.
line.friends.gift.plain.2: Oh. Well, thank you. It's not the what, it's the who.
line.friends.gift.plain.3: {0}, thanks for thinking of me. I'll find it a good home.
line.friends.gift.plain.4: Hm. Unexpected. But it's nice that you thought of me.
line.friends.gift.again.1: Another present? You're spoiling me! Not every day, {0}.
line.friends.gift.again.2: No, no, that's enough for today. Keep it, we'll see tomorrow.
line.friends.gift.again.3: You've already given me something today. Just sit with me a minute instead.
friends.host.holm.name: Viktor Sergeyevich Holm
friends.tea.holm.welcome: Holm sets two glasses in metal holders on the table and a bowl of ship's biscuit. He brews the tea strong, the navigator's way, and turns the table so that we can both see the east. "No sugar aboard. There's biscuit and there's the forecast."
friends.tea.holm.q1: About the storm in the painting
friends.tea.holm.a1: Biscay, seventy-four. Three days of waves higher than the mast, and the Ladoga kept going and going, the old tub. I was at the wheel and I prayed, though I was in the Komsomol. "All alive": I wrote that in when we got home. The most important line of my life, {0}.
friends.tea.holm.a2: Kostya. We were at the naval college together. Forty years we've played by post, a move a month, sometimes one every two months. His last card came a long while ago, and I look in the box every day. He isn't ill, no. He's thinking. Kostya always took his time over the queen.
friends.tea.holm.a3: Nina. We danced in Riga in sixty-one, and a year later I went off on my first voyage. For thirty years she waited for me on shore, and I kept coming and going. Now I'm ashore for good, and there's nobody to wait for. That's why I watch the sunrise: at least somebody turns up on time.
friends.tea.holm.bye: Watch handed over, {0}. Drop in again: the door isn't locked. On board ship we never locked the cabins.
friends.tea.holm.invite:
Ship's boy,

I invite you to navy tea {0}, at {1}. When the bell strikes, come in: the door, as you know, isn't locked. I'll tell you how a real watch log is kept. I don't promise sugar; I promise ship's biscuit.

V. S. Holm
friends.host.okada.name: Lev Markovich Okada
friends.tea.okada.welcome: Okada pushes the tubes marked YELLOW and MORE YELLOW to the edge of the table and sets out two cups: one with a blue rim, one with a chipped handle, which he keeps for himself. On the saucer, dry rings and a slice of lemon. "Asya always put lemon in. So do I, though I don't like it."
friends.tea.okada.q2: About the woman at the window
friends.tea.okada.a1: Because it's different every time, {0}. Today the sea has a green tinge; tomorrow it'll be like tin. I don't paint the window, I paint the day that stood in it. And besides... one day the sun will set differently, and I want to be at the window with a brush in my hand.
friends.tea.okada.a2: That's Asya. I painted her from behind because she didn't like sitting: "Lyova, I'm not a haystack." I remember her face without a picture. But the light on her cheek that day was such that I was afraid to move. Forty years have gone by, and it's still there.
friends.tea.okada.a3: My only exhibition. They printed my name last and small; eleven people came to the opening, and ten of them were Asya. She stood in front of each painting for ten minutes on her own. It was she who ringed my name in red in the catalogue. She said: "So you can find yourself."
friends.tea.okada.bye: Thank you for sitting with me, {0}. Tonight I'll finish number eleven hundred and thirteen: with you at the table it'll come out warmer.
friends.tea.okada.invite:
My friend,

Come to tea {0}, at {1}. That's just when the light I paint for begins. The cup with the blue rim is waiting for you, and so is the lemon. If you're late, no matter: the window isn't going anywhere.

L. M. Okada
friends.host.singh.name: Ilmar Singh
friends.tea.singh.welcome: Ilmar clears a space between the soldering iron and the contact log and sets out two enamel mugs. Tea without sugar, and dry rings from the drawer where the valves lie wrapped in newspaper. Over the table the air hisses softly, like a kettle that never boils.
friends.tea.singh.q3: About the mark on the window
friends.tea.singh.a1: Gunnar is the closest person in the world to me, and he lives a kilometre away. For twenty years we talked only on the air: it's easier, nobody sees you get flustered. The records for him are still tied up with string. Handing something over in person takes a different kind of courage altogether, {0}.
friends.tea.singh.a2: A warden goes round the tower every evening. Lamps, doors, taps: that's easy. But sometimes somebody's crying behind a door, and then I don't knock. I leave a chocolate and walk on. In the morning the wrapper's in the bin by the lift. That means the round went well.
friends.tea.singh.a3: On midsummer day the sun sets exactly into that mark. I wait for it with a watch, like a call sign on the air. Twelve years running, it hasn't been a minute late. If only everybody I talk to were that punctual, {0}...
friends.tea.singh.bye: Over and out, {0}. But not quite: frequency 7055, if you need me.
friends.tea.singh.invite:
Come in!

I invite you to tea at the Capsule Tower {0}, at {1}. Come up to my floor: the door will be ajar and the radio on. I have exactly two mugs, and from today the second one is yours.

Ilmar
friends.host.kravets.name: Nora Kravets
friends.tea.kravets.welcome: Nora shoves her textbooks aside and sets out two odd mugs: one with her village's crest, the other from the hostel, with a chipped rim. The tea is herbal, her mum's, from the parcel, and there are thin slices of mountain cheese. "It smells of home. Well, mine."
friends.tea.kravets.a1: The moon pulls the water, the sun pulls it too, and our coast turns it round besides, like a spoon in a glass. Three times I got it wrong, and once I nearly cried over the exercise book. Then I went to the pier and looked at the water. It turns out sometimes you just have to look first and count afterwards.
friends.tea.kravets.a2: One crane for every day by the sea. Granny used to say: fold a thousand and your wish comes true. I haven't decided which wish yet. Maybe for Mum to stop worrying. Maybe for the sea never to get boring. So far it hasn't got boring one bit, {0}.
friends.tea.kravets.a3: That's our choir, from the village. Mum sings the second part; you can hear her if you listen really hard. I put the record on when I'm homesick, and then straight away the tape of the sea. It's as if the mountains come down to the water. I suppose that's what my home looks like now.
friends.tea.kravets.bye: Thanks for coming, {0}. Tonight I'll fold a crane with your name on it.
friends.tea.kravets.invite:
Hi!

Mum sent another parcel, and I can't eat that much cheese on my own. Come to tea {0}, at {1}. I promise not to talk about tides. Well, almost.

Nora
friends.host.okafor.name: Gunnar Okafor
friends.tea.okafor.welcome: Gunnar lifts the headphones off his pillow, blows the dust off two mugs and opens a jar of cherry jam. He pours the tea to a record from the "For sun" shelf. "It's written on my map: tea with jam is the best connection."
friends.tea.okafor.a1: Because music is weather too, {0}. Rain wants Chopin, wind wants a march, sun wants anything at all, so long as there's a trumpet in it. Put on the wrong one and the day goes crooked: tried and tested. "For sun" is the fattest shelf: I'm an optimist, even living on the Baltic.
friends.tea.okafor.a2: Half a year I searched the world for it: I asked Tiksi, I asked Valparaíso. And it was playing in the jukebox at the Saucer, round the corner. That's how it often goes: the thing you need is playing close by, only the interference keeps you from hearing it. Now I put it on when Ilmar's ill.
friends.tea.okafor.a3: I was a radio operator on a cargo ship for ten years. The navigator gave me the scarf when I signed off ashore: "So you'll sleep like in a swell." Ashore I couldn't sleep at all for a long time. Then I put up an aerial, and the world started rocking again, the way it should.
friends.tea.okafor.bye: Come again, {0}. On the air, politely; as a guest, just as you are.
friends.tea.okafor.invite:
Helper,

I've opened a new jar of jam, and it never opens properly without a guest. Come to tea {0}, at {1}. We'll pick the record by the weather.

Gunnar
friends.host.tadesse.name: Valentina Tadesse
friends.tea.tadesse.welcome: Valentina sets out cups with painted fish, each with its own name on the bottom. Hamish brings sandwiches from the kitchen and the yellow jar: "These are my lemon drops. But guests are allowed." The aquarium blows bubbles as if it wants to join the table too.
friends.tea.tadesse.q3: About the portrait with the rod
friends.tea.tadesse.a1: Fish don't live long, but I don't throw the names away. Hamlet was the first, back in the sixties. Now we have Hamlet the Seventh, and he has the family temper, believe me. The rest live on in the paintings. Nothing can happen to them there, {0}.
friends.tea.tadesse.a2: Fifty years I've painted fish, because fish don't ask whether it's a likeness. The sun will. My granddaughter asks: "Granny, paint the sun." The ground on the canvas has gone yellow with waiting. Hamish says it'll turn into the sun by itself soon, without me.
friends.tea.tadesse.a3: Our first date. He invited me fishing; nothing bit for three hours, and he kept smiling as if something was biting. I thought then: with a man like that, even fifty years without a catch wouldn't be frightening. And that's how it turned out. Hamish, don't listen, I'm not talking to you.
friends.tea.tadesse.bye: Come whenever you like, {0}. No need to ring. And don't feed the fish!
friends.tea.tadesse.invite:
Dear boy,

We'll expect you to tea in the studio {0}, at {1}. Hamish promises fish soup if they bite and sandwiches if they don't. He promises lemon drops too, but there I don't believe him.

V. Tadesse
friends.host.okonkwo.name: Yasmin Okonkwo
friends.tea.okonkwo.welcome: Yasmin sets clay cups on the table, a little lopsided and all different: Mads made them, Emiliano helped. On the plate, whale-shaped biscuits, one with two tails. Emiliano sits down beside me and watches sternly to make sure I take that one.
friends.tea.okonkwo.q1: About the whale on the wheel
friends.tea.okonkwo.a1: The whale is waiting for Dad, and we wait along with the whale. I water it every morning like a flower so it won't crack. Emiliano wanted it to have a second tail; Mads said, "All right, let it have two." Once it's fired, it'll be the most crooked and most loved whale in the world.
friends.tea.okonkwo.a2: Mads painted it while I was cutting his hair. I told him to keep still, and he kept his brush moving. It's a good likeness, isn't it? He's no artist, he just looked for a long time. Nobody has ever given me anything better, {0}.
friends.tea.okonkwo.a3: Emiliano crosses off a square every evening, and sometimes in the morning too, just in case. Two weeks is three hundred and thirty-six hours; Mads counts them too. Never mind, we're used to it. But when he comes home, we have a holiday all weekend, and clay on every floor.
friends.tea.okonkwo.bye: Come again, {0}. And if you need a haircut: the promenade, the chair by the window, no queue for you.
friends.tea.okonkwo.invite:
Hi!

Emiliano told me to write that he invites "the one who knows about the whale" to tea {0}, at {1}. The whale biscuits are in the oven already; he shaped the tails himself. Come to the studio: the door's open.

Yasmin and Emiliano
friends.host.santos.name: Vera and Emil Santos
friends.tea.santos.welcome: Vera sets four cups on the kitchen table, a fifth for me and a bottle for Noel. Emil cuts the pie into seven pieces: "The seventh is Noel's, to grow into." Lina and Timo argue in whispers about who'll sit next to the guest, and both do.
friends.tea.santos.q3: About "Our first day by the sea"
friends.tea.santos.a1: Lina! Somebody left a hint in her exercise book, and she swears she doesn't know who. Timo demands a recount, and Emil does the dishes, grumbling that the judge was bribed. The judge, by the way, is me. And I won't tell anyone that the handwriting in the book is a boy's, {0}.
friends.tea.santos.a2: That's Timo. He ticks off every bird and is cross that albatrosses don't fly here. He also drew a sun bird there that he saw in a dream. Now he thinks you'll find it, since you're from the bird club. Don't let him down straight away, will you?
friends.tea.santos.a3: We came here with one suitcase and two children; Noel wasn't born yet. We sat on the shore the whole first day and went nowhere, not even to see the flat. Emil painted it a year later, from memory. He says it was sunnier then. I think we were just younger.
friends.tea.santos.bye: Come again, {0}! Only next time you do the dishes: house rules.
friends.tea.santos.invite:
Hello!

All the Santoses (five of them, counting Noel) invite you to tea and pie {0}, at {1}. Timo has questions ready about birds, Lina about Venus. No need to take your shoes off: we've five pairs in the hall as it is.

Vera and Emil
friends.host.girma.name: Daisuke Girma
friends.tea.girma.welcome: Daisuke puts the teapot on the table, the very one from the still life, and slices apples, red with a yellow cheek. Tomo brings a third cup and sets it at his mum's place: "That's for Friday. But it can stand there for now."
friends.tea.girma.q1: About the sun on the night chart
friends.tea.girma.q3: When does Tomo's mum come home?
friends.tea.girma.a1: Tomo was five. I told him there's no sun at night, and he got upset and drew it right in the middle of the constellations. Afterwards I lay awake half the night thinking: he's right, you know. It's always there, just on the other side. It's like that with people who are far away too, {0}.
friends.tea.girma.a2: Three years without missing a day. In the morning, before the market, five minutes at the telescope, with the filter: Tomo checks. The spots come and go, like customers. Every evening I write to Nino how many there were. She says they're the strangest love letters in the world.
friends.tea.girma.a3: On Friday evening, by train. That day Tomo draws from the morning on, and I try not to be late back from the market: it says so on the calendar. Yesterday another little star appeared there, a tiny one. Nobody in the family owns up to it. Well, let it stay.
friends.tea.girma.bye: Come again, {0}, and on a clear day have a look through the telescope. Only with the filter: Tomo will make sure.
friends.tea.girma.invite:
Hello!

Come to us for tea {0}, at {1}. There'll be apples from the market and, if the sky allows, fresh spots on the sun. Tomo says he'll draw you, but only if you sit still.

Daisuke and Tomo
friends.host.aoki.name: Rimma Aoki
friends.tea.aoki.welcome: Rimma clears the patterns off the table, sticks her needle into the pincushion and sets out two cups from different sets: "Not one too many: each is from somebody." With the tea, poppy-seed rusks and honey, yellow "as at six in the morning".
friends.tea.aoki.q1: About the suns on the hem
friends.tea.aoki.a1: A girl from the market brought linen and asked for a plain dress, for her graduation. She didn't ask for suns. But she has the face of someone who meets the dawn every morning. I sewed the last sun with that yellow, "as at seven in the evening". Somebody laid the swatch in the right place. You don't know who, {0}?
friends.tea.aoki.a2: Every patch is from somebody's dress: a wedding dress, a school dress, the one they wore to see someone off. I've sewn for half the town, and from each of them I kept a scrap. Under this quilt it's never lonely. And the yellow in the middle is mine. I'm still finding out what it really is.
friends.tea.aoki.a3: The Chaika is older than me; it was Mum's. Mum used to say you mustn't rush a machine, or a person either. I stuck that note on it the year I did everything at a run and had to redo everything. Now we both sew slowly. And we hardly ever unpick a thing.
friends.tea.aoki.bye: Drop in again, {0}. A button to sew on or a sleeve to take up: come to me, no queue.
friends.tea.aoki.invite:
Hello!

The dress with the suns is finished and gone to its graduate, and at last I have a free evening. Come to tea {0}, at {1}. There'll be honey, there'll be rusks, and I promise not to switch on the machine.

R. Aoki
friends.tea.served.1: The tea is poured. Steam rises over the cups, and the talk begins by itself.
friends.tea.served.2: My host moves a cup and a plate over to me. It smells of tea and of someone else's cosy home.
friends.tea.served.3: On the table, tea and something to go with it. Outside the sea murmurs; in here it's quiet and warm.

friends.festival.diary: {1}. A friend found me in the crowd: {0}. We went round together after that, and the holiday became twice as short and twice as good.
friends.outing.toast: {0} waves to you: the whole family's here.
friends.diary.title: People
friends.diary.empty: Empty so far. I should say hello more often: in this town everyone becomes an acquaintance sooner or later.

friends.gift.none: Nothing in my pockets to give.
